differences.title: 1. CONFIGURATION
differences.leftDesc: Caddy's Caddyfile or JSON config is declarative. It automatically obtains and renews TLS certificates via Let's Encrypt, simplifying HTTPS setup significantly.
differences.rightDesc: NGINX uses an imperative configuration style with directives. TLS certificate management requires separate tools like Certbot, demanding manual configuration and renewal.

differences.title: 2. EASE OF USE
differences.leftDesc: Caddy aims for zero configuration for common use cases. It intelligently serves static files or proxies requests with minimal user input needed.
differences.rightDesc: NGINX requires explicit configuration for most tasks. Achieving optimal performance often involves fine-tuning worker processes, connections, and buffer sizes.

differences.title: 3. PROTOCOL SUPPORT
differences.leftDesc: Caddy has first-class support for HTTP/3 built-in, leveraging the QUIC protocol for improved performance over UDP, especially on lossy networks.
differences.rightDesc: NGINX supports HTTP/3 through third-party modules or specific builds, often requiring compilation flags and additional configuration for QUIC integration.

differences.title: 4. PLUGIN ARCHITECTURE
differences.leftDesc: Caddy's plugins are written in Go and integrated directly into the binary. This provides tight coupling and efficient execution.
differences.rightDesc: NGINX plugins (modules) are typically written in C and dynamically loaded. This offers flexibility but can sometimes lead to compatibility issues.

differences.title: 5. PERFORMANCE
differences.leftDesc: Caddy is built in Go, offering excellent performance with efficient concurrency. Its modern design is optimized for current web traffic patterns.
differences.rightDesc: NGINX is renowned for its highly optimized, event-driven, asynchronous architecture, excelling at handling a massive number of concurrent connections with low memory footprint.

differences.title: 6. ADAPTABILITY
differences.leftDesc: Caddy offers a dynamic configuration API, allowing changes to be applied without restarting the server. This is great for orchestration.
differences.rightDesc: NGINX is a Swiss Army knife: web server, reverse proxy, load balancer, mail proxy, and static content server, highly configurable for diverse roles.

differences.title: 7. COMMUNITY & ECOSYSTEM
differences.leftDesc: Caddy has a vibrant and rapidly growing community, with active development and increasing adoption, supported by the Linux Foundation.
differences.rightDesc: NGINX boasts one of the largest and most mature ecosystems in web infrastructure, with extensive documentation, community support, and widespread enterprise adoption.
